text:
ana: Quick thought — can we add a lightweight "compatibility sweep" to the onboarding pipeline? not full bench, just a fast probe set to catch obvious regressions early. idea: ~200 short prompts across categories, run on runtime/quantized/cpu fallback variants.

dave: sounds useful. how do you pick the 200? random or curated? cost targets? :money_with_wings:

maria: curated + stratified. pick golden cases per capability bucket (summarization, code, Q/A, chit-chat) + a few adversarial examples. deterministic seed so runs are comparable.

kelly: we should reuse smokehouse infra if possible. tag the sweep as "light-sweep" so rollout tooling can gate on it. if failure rate > X% block canary.

ana: (typo) ana: yes — thresholding is key. propose: fail if any of these trigger: 1) >5% token-level perplexity regression vs baseline, 2) >2% exact-answer drop on golden Q/A, 3) large latency tail increase (>100ms p95). these thresholds can be tuning knobs per model family.

dave: how do we measure perplexity fast? full eval is expensive. maybe proxy metrics: token-kl on a small sample + logprob shift on golden prompts.

maria: agree. also add a simple output-shape/format validator for structured outputs (json schema). that catches common breaking changes when tokenization/decoding differs.

kelly: config idea for the job (pseudo):
```json
{
  "job": "light-sweep",
  "model": "${MODEL}",
  "variants": ["runtime", "quantized", "cpu-fallback"],
  "input_set": "light-probes-v1",
  "metrics": ["kl_proxy", "gold_exact", "p95_latency"],
  "thresholds": {"kl_proxy": 0.1, "gold_exact": 0.02, "p95_latency_ms": 100}
}
```

ana: we also need a cheap KV-cache warmup pattern — some models look fine cold but blow up after a few tokens. maybe include a short prefix boost for latency tests.

dave: good call. add a 32-token warmup and run the latency probe separately.

maria: what about integration with rollouts? if light-sweep fails, mark model as "hold" in registry and prevent hosted canary. engineers can override with a forced flag + manual signoff.

kelly: operationally: add an entry in the console UI to surface light-sweep diffs (small sparkline + top 3 failing prompts). that makes triage quick. :eyes:

ana: who wants to own the initial prototype? i can sketch the probe set and seeds. need someone to wire the job into smokehouse and expose the signal to model-registry.

maria: I can wire the registry bits and the UI surface.

dave: i can hook up the kl_proxy and latency probes into bench runner.

kelly: i'll doc the rollout flow and add the canary gating rule.

sre-bot: bench-job queued: light-sweep-172861 (eta ~ 12m) :gear:

ana: sweet — i'll drop the initial probe list in the repo today and open a short RFC with config examples.

dave: :thumbsup:

maria: thanks, all.

kelly: low-risk, high-signal — love it.
